Package de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.config

Class OpenApiConfig

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.config.OpenApiConfig
@Configuration public class OpenApiConfig extends Object
OpenAPI document metadata for the published REST API.

Built programmatically rather than through annotations so the info.version tracks the application version from the build (@project.version@ filtered into application.yaml) instead of being a second place to bump on every release.

Two authentication schemes are declared because the app runs one of two mutually exclusive security chains depending on the active profile (see SecurityConfig / KeycloakSecurityConfig): basicAuth in the default (dev) profiles and bearerAuth (a Keycloak-issued JWT) under the keycloak profile. Both are offered as alternatives on every operation; a client uses whichever matches the deployment it talks to.

Author:
peter haller

    • stableOperationIds

      @Bean public org.springdoc.core.customizers.OperationCustomizer stableOperationIds()
      Gives every operation a stable, unique operationId derived deterministically from its controller and method: <resource>_<method>, e.g. company_create or projectInstance_startForProject. This replaces springdoc's default (the bare method name, with _1/_2 suffixes appended in registration order whenever names collide across controllers — and create/update/delete/getById collide several times here). Those default ids are order-dependent and therefore unfit to freeze: a generated client's method names would shift when an unrelated endpoint is added. The scheme here is self-maintaining — a new endpoint gets a stable id with no annotation to remember — and the <resource>_ prefix makes the ids unique across controllers while method names stay unique within one. Part of the 1.0 API-stability promise; see the class Javadoc.
